data.name: Darvik
data.gender_notes: Darvik is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Darvik is a powerful god associated with thunder and lightning. His name symbolizes his rule over the sky and his mighty power to strike with lightning bolts. The name Darvik carries the meaning “Ruler of the Thunder” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Darvik usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the thunder and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Darvik belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler of the Thunder.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Darvik total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: In Indian mythology, Darvik is known as the god of thunder and lightning. He is an important Hindu deity, especially revered in the Maharashtra region. Hindu festivals such as the Ganesh Chaturthi and Dussehra are believed to be influenced by Darvik's power, as these festivals involve the use of thunderous drumming, cracking firecrackers, and lighting of oil lamps to ward off darkness and invite prosperity and good fortune. Darvik is also believed to have the power to bring rains, which are crucial for agriculture, and his image is often found at village and temple water tanks.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Darvik is derived from the Sanskrit word "Darshan," meaning divine vision or sight. It symbolizes one's inner journey towards gaining spiritual wisdom and enlightenment, as well as the ability to perceive the divine in all aspects of life.

vedic_reference.note: The name 'Darvik' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'darshan' (radiant) and 'vik' (warrior) to mean 'Radiant Warrior'.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Darvik is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a king in the kingdom of Kalinga. The name Darvik carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
